lesson.title: 911 – Procedure 104: Interim Status Codes (10-80 to 10-89)
objectives: Explain what interim status codes are and when they are used.
Correctly apply codes 10-80 through 10-89 while units remain on assignments.
Describe how interim codes affect service time and unit alarms.
Avoid mis-applying interim/final codes to the wrong jobs by displaying the correct event.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes interim status codes according to Procedure 104?

choices.text: They are used only after a unit has completely finished an assignment, including all paperwork.
They show the present status of a job while the unit is still on the assignment, and service time continues to run.
They permanently mark a unit as out of service.
They replace all final disposition codes.

questions.solution: Procedure 104 states that interim codes show the present status of a job while the unit is still on assignment, and service time continues until a final disposition is entered.

questions.stem: A unit wants to indicate that they have arrived at the location of the assignment. Which interim code should they use?
questions.solution: 10-84 is specifically defined as ARRIVED AT SCENE.

questions.stem: Service time on an event stops as soon as any interim status code is entered.
Entering an interim disposition will also remove a Unit Alarm for the unit concerned.
Code 10-85 indicates that a unit NEEDS __________ UNIT(S) and should specify if a supervisor is needed.
Procedure 104 warns that interim or final codes may end up on the wrong job if the dispatcher does not first __________ the correct event before entering the code.
Match each interim status code with its correct meaning.
Match each description with whether it refers to INTERIM STATUS or FINAL DISPOSITIONS.
answer: Service time continues to run and the unit is still on the job.
Unit has completed the assignment, including all paperwork and notifications.
